title: Soft tissue lump — when to suspect sarcoma

guidelineVersions: NICE NG12 Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (last updated 15 April 2026)
British Sarcoma Group UK guidelines for the management of soft tissue sarcomas (2024)

brief.scenario: You are the core surgical trainee. 48-year-old; left upper thigh lump noticed 5 months ago, now 7 cm, deep to fascia, firm and relatively fixed; mild intermittent ache, normal distal pulses and power. Ultrasound: 7.1 × 5.4 × 4.8 cm deep heterogeneous vascular solid mass, indeterminate/suspicious for soft tissue neoplasm.
brief.task: Interpret the supplied clinical and ultrasound information about an enlarging left thigh lump. Explain the differential, safe investigation, referral pathway and immediate next steps to the examiner.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Surgical assessment clinic; a 48-year-old with a left thigh mass
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Treating a painless lump, or an uncertain ultrasound, as permission for an unplanned excision.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: This is an enlarging deep 7-cm soft tissue mass with concerning ultrasound findings. I would refer through the sarcoma pathway, not excise it locally.

flow: State clinical frame and identify the report’s key abnormality.
Interrogate the missing context and interpret evidence.
Explain differential and limitations, without overdiagnosis.
State safe pathway, investigations and specialist escalation.
Handle the new cue and close with explicit next steps.

grid.label: Opening and clinical frame
grid.fail: Starts brusquely, calls the lesion a lipoma without seeing data.
grid.borderline: Introduces role but does not establish whether mass is enlarging.
grid.pass: Uses the growth, depth and size details to raise concern for sarcoma.
grid.high: Frames an enlarging deep mass as potential sarcoma, explicitly avoiding an unplanned excision.

grid.label: Risk features
grid.fail: Says absence of pain excludes cancer.
grid.borderline: Mentions growth but misses depth and size.
grid.pass: Identifies 7-cm deep, enlarging thigh lump as concerning.
grid.high: Explains that size >5 cm and deep location increase concern, while growth alone drives NG12 urgent ultrasound.

grid.label: Ultrasound reading
grid.borderline: Notes heterogeneous finding but no next step.
grid.pass: Recognises deep heterogeneous vascular solid lesion as suspicious and requests sarcoma-team review.
grid.high: Separates ultrasound triage from definitive tissue diagnosis and requests specialist planned imaging.

grid.label: Referral pathway
grid.borderline: Requests ultrasound again without addressing concerning first scan.
grid.pass: Uses suspected-cancer pathway to specialist sarcoma service because scan is suggestive.
grid.high: Explicitly references urgent ultrasound within 2 weeks for enlarging unexplained lump and specialist referral for suspicious/uncertain scans with persisting concern.

grid.label: Biopsy planning
grid.fail: Offers office excision to establish diagnosis.
grid.borderline: Mentions biopsy without specifying specialist planning.
grid.pass: States that MRI and core biopsy planning belong in specialist sarcoma pathway; no unplanned excision.
grid.high: Explains imaging before planned image-guided core biopsy and positioning of biopsy tract with surgical team.

grid.label: Differential and scope
grid.borderline: Names benign and malignant causes but does not interpret case pattern.
grid.pass: Considers lipoma, haematoma and sarcoma, treating case as malignant until evaluated.
grid.high: Acknowledges not all >5-cm masses are sarcoma, but clinical context precludes reassurance.

grid.label: Neurological and vascular function
grid.pass: Assesses pain, numbness, weakness and distal vascular symptoms, prompting examination.
grid.high: Integrates preserved pulses with no assurance about pathology, and checks evolving neurovascular compromise.

grid.label: Safety and patient information
grid.borderline: Says cancer is possible without pathway or timeline.
grid.pass: Explains urgent referral without announcing a diagnosis; records and communicates plan.
grid.high: Handles anxiety, explains why biopsy should be specialised, ensures follow-up and safety net.

grid.label: Curveball and finish
grid.fail: On growth in two weeks, still books elective removal.
grid.borderline: Acknowledges rapid change but leaves routine appointment.
grid.pass: On report mass has doubled over 2 weeks, promptly contacts sarcoma team and escalates urgency.
grid.high: Communicates rapidly progressive symptoms to specialist same day and ensures prompt evaluation for compression or bleeding.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What concerns you most about this lump?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It has enlarged over five months, is deep and measures seven centimetres. I would consider sarcoma and avoid removing it without specialist assessment.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Growth, depth, size and fixation are relevant. I would assess neurological or vascular symptoms as well.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A heterogeneous vascular deep solid mass is suspicious; ultrasound cannot establish subtype.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: NG12 says to consider urgent ultrasound for a growing unexplained mass, and a suspected-cancer referral when findings are suspicious or uncertain with concern.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Would you biopsy or excise it today?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No local excision. Specialist imaging and planned core biopsy are needed.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Lipoma, haematoma and malignant soft tissue tumour, but the findings require sarcoma exclusion.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What symptoms would you ask about next?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Pain, numbness, weakness, skin change and vascular symptoms.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What would you tell this patient?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The ultrasound is concerning and needs an urgent specialist opinion; it does not prove cancer.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: New information: it has doubled in size over two weeks and feels tight. What now?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would contact the specialist service promptly today, update the referral and assess new neurovascular symptoms.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What concerns you most about this lump?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: An enlarging, 7-cm, deep solid thigh mass requires prompt sarcoma assessment; pain is neither necessary nor sufficient for malignancy.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Which features are significant?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Its deep location, relatively fixed nature and growth are concerning. I would document distal power, sensation and perfusion and not confuse intact pulses with benignity.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Interpret this ultrasound report.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The report says indeterminate or suspicious for soft tissue neoplasm. That requires referral; imaging triages but does not give definitive histology.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What pathway do you use?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: This has already met the ultrasound criterion and the report remains suspicious: I would arrange the sarcoma suspected-cancer pathway and make sure the result is acknowledged.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Would you biopsy or excise it today?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would not biopsy or excise it outside the specialist plan. The sarcoma MDT coordinates further imaging and biopsy tract planning to preserve definitive treatment options.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What are your alternatives?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Benign mimics exist, but the accelerating growth and deep solid vascular appearance make unplanned reassurances inappropriate.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What symptoms would you ask about next?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would ask about progressive neurological symptoms, tightness, swelling, skin involvement and function. Compression warrants prompt examination.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What would you tell this patient?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would explain the uncertainty, the reason for an urgent referral and the importance of not having a casual “lump removal”; I would document who owns follow-up.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: New information: it has doubled in size over two weeks and feels tight. What now?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That is an important change: I would assess for acute compression or bleeding, contact the sarcoma team the same day and ensure the urgency and safety-net advice reach the patient.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Please summarise your next action in one sentence.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will contact the sarcoma team today and document who follows up.

failures.move: Delays specialist referral for a suspicious deep growing solid mass.
Performs unplanned local excision or biopsy without specialist planning.
Ignores rapid enlargement with possible compression.
failures.consequence: May miss acute nerve or vascular compromise.

recovery.when: If you called it a lipoma too soon
recovery.line: I called it a lipoma too soon. Growth, depth and this ultrasound make sarcoma possible; I will stop any local excision plan and refer to the sarcoma service.

recovery.when: If the new rapid growth is reported
recovery.line: The new rapid growth changes my urgency. I will examine distal neurological and vascular function and contact the specialist pathway today.

knowledge.fact: For an adult with an unexplained lump that is increasing in size, NG12 says consider an urgent direct-access ultrasound, performed within two weeks.
Ultrasound suspicious for sarcoma or uncertain with continued clinical concern means considering a suspected cancer pathway referral.
Large (>5 cm), deep or growing masses increase concern but no single feature makes a histological diagnosis.
Suspected sarcoma is evaluated in a specialist pathway with imaging and planned tissue sampling.
Core biopsy and biopsy-tract planning are usually specialist-directed, avoiding an unplanned excision.
Rapid enlargement warrants prompt re-discussion with the specialist team and assessment for compression or bleeding.

recall.think: An enlarging deep solid mass is potentially sarcoma until specialist investigation.
recall.say: “I will refer this suspicious 7-cm thigh mass through the sarcoma pathway.”
do: Check size, depth, growth, ultrasound, neurovascular findings and specialist referral.

numbers.meaning: >5 cm is a concern flag, not a diagnostic cut-off

recall.trap: Do not perform an unplanned local excision or rely on absence of pain.
recall.finish: Document the plan, urgency and person responsible for contacting the patient.
